item.title: The Crisis of Protection in Muslim Countries
item.description: By K S T Qureshi The most basic moral claim of any government is that it exists to protect the lives, dignity, and security of the people under its authority. Political philosophers from Thomas Hobbes to John Locke, and jurists across civilisations, have agreed on this foundational premise where individuals surrender certain freedoms to the state in exchange for safety from violence, chaos, and arbitrary harm. When a government fails in this obligation, or worse, becomes a direct source of fear
